input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative access/use grant, but it runs to "the Company" alone: no affiliates, no contractors acting on our behalf, and no written-notice mechanic to add them. That fails a material term of the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transferability. The gap is not merely one of silence: Section 10.3 (p0063) provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which affirmatively excludes our affiliates and contractors from exercising the Section 1.4 rights and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger. Section 10.3 is otherwise a standard binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause; it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but does not itself grant an affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it only weakly supports the second fallback element and cannot cure the missing affiliate and contractor coverage. The redline makes the smallest edits to reach the preferred position: it extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and carves those parties out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3. The comment offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback. The grant is not expressed to be revocable at HDI's discretion, so no revocability deletion is needed, and the term/termination mechanics are addressed under the term rule.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to the Company's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and to a successor in an M&A transaction, and carve them out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (and to a successor in a merger or sale of the business), since our group and outsourced providers need to operate and monitor the Site; our playbook requires affiliate and contractor coverage plus successor transferability. We also carved those parties out of the "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" language in Section 10.3, which as drafted would exclude them; if you prefer, we can accept affiliates being added on written notice to HDI.

ops.newText: HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information. The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 may be exercised by the Company, its affiliates (meaning any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with the Company) and any contractors acting on the Company's behalf, and may be transferred to any successor to the Company's business by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
